note: Golden wire contract for the sign-in bridge's APP DOOR (DDR 0246, ADR 0236; Ben's rulings on idss #1666 and #1669). matou-app copies THIS file so neither side guesses the wire. Values are illustrative; the fields, paths, statuses and refusal kinds are the contract. Snake_case on the wire.
_copied_from: idss internal/idp/testdata/app-door-golden.json @ cb183eac (copied for matou-app #663; panel handover added by idss#1939)

sign_in_site.rule: ONE string is the sign-in site: the descriptor's signin.url == the ask's door == the address the verifier binds. It is the bridge's own sign-in address.

ask.response_note: This is an ORDINARY service sign-in: it carries NEITHER sealing_key NOR ek= (see panel below). The negative case is as much of the contract as the positive one.

deep_link_params_note: ek= rides ONLY a control-panel challenge whose code offered a sealing key (see panel below); an ordinary service sign-in carries the other six and no ek=.

present.url: the ask's present_url, verbatim — never derived from door
present.request_note: The plain (non-panel) present request carries NO sealed_passcode. A panel unlock adds one — see panel.present.request below.

sealed_box_refused.when: a sealed_passcode arrives on an ordinary service sign-in, OR on a panel challenge whose code carried no ek — there is no key it could have been sealed to. Caught before the verifier; nothing is stored or relayed.

panel.note: The control-panel passcode relay (ADR 0282 d.6 + its 2026-09-27 #1938 amendment, PU-A2u). The panel tab mints a throwaway Ed25519 Signer in tab memory; its verkey qb64 rides ek= as the sealing key, and the steward's phone seals their passcode to it with signify's Encrypter (a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher). The door relays ek= and the cipher as OPAQUE strings — it validates NEITHER. These fields appear ONLY on a control-panel unlock; an ordinary service sign-in (ask.response, present.request above) carries none of them.

challenge.sealing_key_note: the tab's Ed25519 verkey qb64, echoed from ?ek= on the mint; a public key, never a secret — it rides the URL by design, the passcode never does.

present.request_note: sealed_passcode is a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher (1AAH…) the door cannot open. It rides ONLY a panel challenge that offered a sealing key.
present.sealed_box_refused: see present.sealed_box_refused above — a box without a sealing key is refused 400 sealed-box-refused
present.second_box_spent: see present.spent_challenge above — a SECOND box for the same challenge hits the single-use guard: 409 spent
present.box_after_expiry: see present.expired_challenge above — a box after the two-minute life: 410 expired

status_poll.handover_note: handover is the same ciphertext, handed to the tab EXACTLY ONCE then deleted (omitempty). The SECOND poll omits it — no field ever leaks whether one existed, so an ordinary sign-in is byte-identical to a panel unlock after the box is taken.
